artworks.title: Phyllis and Demophoon
artworks.description: Burne-Jones' Birmingham canvas: Phyllis, transformed into an almond tree, clasps the returning Demophon — Theseus' son who abandoned her and found her changed. Pre-Raphaelite myth turns the Athenian prince's Thracian love into a tree-embrace of forgiveness and desire.

artworks.title: The Tree of Forgiveness
artworks.description: A later Burne-Jones reworking of Phyllis and Demophon: the almond-tree nymph still holds the Athenian king. The painting keeps Demophon's afterlife as the lover who returned too late — and was forgiven in bark and blossom.

artworks.title: Phyllis and Demophoön
artworks.description: Waterhouse's Phyllis and Demophon restages the reunion at the almond tree — Demophon of Athens as Pre-Raphaelite errant lover, caught by the woman he left.

popCulture.title: Demophon of Athens
popCulture.description: Son of Theseus and Phaedra; Athenian king who loved Phyllis of Thrace — and, in some tellings, brought the Palladium or Heracles' sons home.

popCulture.title: Heroides
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid's letter of Phyllis to Demophoon (Heroides 2) gives the abandoned Thracian princess her voice against Theseus' son.
